title: Add Previous/Next navigation to playlist item modal
summary: When a playlist is playing and reaches a Text or Link item, that item opens in a pop-up window. Before, the pop-up only had an **X** button to close it, so to move on you had to close it and use the reader's controls. Now, while the playlist plays, the pop-up has **Previous** and **Next** buttons at the bottom instead of the **X**, so you can step through the playlist without leaving it. The same pop-up opened outside of playback (for example from a reading plan) still has its **X** and no buttons at the bottom.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If it shows an error or doesn't load, wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the normal site, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

setup.title: Make a test playlist
setup.body:
Open the **Discover** pane, click **+ Create**, then **Playlist**. Type `Nav test` as the title. Then add these four items in this order, using the **Item type** dropdown under **Add item** and clicking **Add item** after each one:
1. **Text**: title `First step`, body text `This is the first step.`
2. **Link**: `https://example.com`, title `Example link` (leave **Embed this link** as it is).
3. **Scripture**: `John 3:16`
4. **Text**: title `Last step`, body text `This is the last step.`
Save the playlist (**Save** or **Save & exit**). The tests below call this the **Nav test** playlist.

setup.title: Know how to start it
setup.body: In the **Discover** pane, find **Nav test** and click its round **Play playlist** button (the ▶ triangle). The tests below call this "play **Nav test**". If a playlist is already playing, stop it first with **Stop** in the bottom toolbar.

sections.title: Stepping through a playing playlist
sections.intro: Do these in order: each one picks up where the last left off.

tests.title: The first step's pop-up shows Previous and Next instead of an X
steps: Play **Nav test**.
Look at the pop-up that opens.
expected: A pop-up titled **First step** opens, showing `This is the first step.`
There is **no X** button in the pop-up's top-right corner.
Under the text there are two buttons: an outlined **Previous** (with a back-skip icon) on the left and a filled **Next** (with a forward-skip icon) on the right.
**Previous** looks faded and does nothing when clicked, because this is the first step.

tests.title: Next moves to the Link step inside the same pop-up
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, with the **First step** pop-up open.
steps: Click **Next** in the pop-up.
expected: The pop-up now shows the **Example link** step (the link, or the embedded page).
It still has **Previous** and **Next** at the bottom and no **X**.
**Previous** is no longer faded.
In the queue list in the Discover pane, the highlighted row moved to the link.

tests.title: Previous goes back a step
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, on the **Example link** step.
steps: Click **Previous** in the pop-up.
expected: The pop-up shows **First step** again, with **Previous** faded.
Click **Next** once more afterwards to get back to **Example link** for the next test.

tests.title: Next onto a Scripture step closes the pop-up and opens the passage
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, on the **Example link** step.
steps: Click **Next** in the pop-up.
expected: The pop-up closes.
The reader shows **John 3** with verse 16 emphasized, as playlists already did before this change.

tests.title: Leaving the Scripture step reopens the pop-up with the buttons
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, reading John 3:16 as part of the playlist.
steps: Use the reader's own next control to move on (the next arrow in the bottom toolbar, or the → key).
expected: The **Last step** pop-up opens, showing `This is the last step.`
It has **Previous** and **Next** at the bottom and no **X**.

tests.title: Next on the last step finishes the playlist
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, on the **Last step** pop-up.
tests.why: On a saved playlist's last step, **Next** stays clickable and finishes the playlist instead of being faded.
steps: Check that **Next** is not faded.
Click **Next**.
expected: A **Playlist finished** window appears saying "You've reached the end of Nav test."
Closing that window stops the playlist, and the **Last step** pop-up is gone too. No pop-up is left stuck on screen.

tests.title: Clicking outside the pop-up still closes it
tests.why: With the **X** gone, clicking the dimmed area around the pop-up is the only way to close it while playing. This checks that it works and that you aren't stuck.
steps: Play **Nav test** again (choose to start over if asked).
When the **First step** pop-up opens, click the dimmed area outside it.
expected: The pop-up closes.
The playlist is still playing (the queue list is still shown in the Discover pane).
Click **Example link** in the queue list: the pop-up opens again on that step, with **Previous** and **Next**.

tests.title: Clicking a step in the queue list opens it with the buttons
steps: Close the pop-up by clicking outside it.
In the queue list, click **Last step**.
expected: The **Last step** pop-up opens with **Previous** and **Next** and no **X**.
Clicking **Previous** goes back to John 3:16 in the reader, and the pop-up closes.

tests.title: The buttons fit and stay visible on a phone-sized screen
steps: Use a phone, or make the browser window narrow (about the width of a phone).
Play **Nav test**.
On the **First step** pop-up, click **Next** to reach **Example link**.
expected: **Previous** and **Next** are both fully visible on one row at the bottom of the pop-up, without text cut off or overlapping.
On the link step, you can still reach both buttons without the page behind the pop-up scrolling instead. Note how it looks if the link's content is tall.

tests.title: The buttons are readable in dark mode
steps: Open **Settings**, then **Display & Theme**, and pick the **Dark** theme.
Play **Nav test** and look at the **First step** pop-up.
expected: The **Next** button's text is easy to read against its filled background.
The outlined **Previous** button is visible against the pop-up (faded, since it's the first step).
Switch back to your usual theme afterwards.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The Playlist finished window still has its normal close button
tests.why: Other pop-ups use the same window code; only playing playlist items should lose the X.
steps: Play **Nav test** and click **Next** until you reach the end, so **Playlist finished** appears.
expected: The **Playlist finished** window looks as it did before: it has its usual way to close, and no **Previous** / **Next** buttons.

tests.title: A Text or Link reading opened from a reading plan keeps its X and has no buttons
tests.before: You need a reading plan that includes a Text or Link reading. If the reading plan editor doesn't let you add one, mark this test **Blocked** and say so.
steps: Stop any playing playlist.
Open the reading plan, find the Text or Link reading, and open it (tap the reading to open its preview).
expected: A pop-up shows the reading's content with an **X** in its top-right corner.
There are no **Previous** / **Next** buttons at the bottom.
Clicking the **X** closes it.

notCovered: Two people in a shared session: the buttons call the same step forward / back as the reader's controls, which already sync between participants, but this plan doesn't check it with two browsers.
The PR's automated tests cover the pop-up's new options (buttons at the bottom, hiding the X) and which buttons are faded.
